scope: Frozen 203 bootstrap READMEs, including their referenced current local contracts.

findings.title: Script language entry points disagree with the root guide
findings.difference: The root guide directs C#/Go/Java authors to Studio/the script API after the TypeScript/Python-only CLI. Studio disables Go and Java, while server authoring validation accepts all five. The referenced OpenAPI createScript description and its generated TypeScript comment still say only TypeScript/Python are built and reject the other three.
findings.correction: State the current entry-point matrix explicitly: CLI TypeScript/Python; Studio TypeScript/Python/C#; API authoring accepts all five subject to configured runner/toolchain capabilities. Align canonical OpenAPI availability text and regenerate derived declarations. Track any Studio expansion as implementation work rather than imply it already exists.
findings.closure: Root instructions and contract availability text agree with the actual selectors/validators; genuine execution acceptance remains a separate gate.

findings.title: Java installation notes deny an existing release pipeline
findings.difference: The installation section says no signing or release pipeline exists. The current workflow packages SDKs, collects artifacts, attests provenance and conditionally publishes GitHub Releases, including Java artifacts produced by package-sdks.sh.
findings.correction: Describe the existing GitHub packaging/attestation/release path and distinguish it from deferred external Maven repository publication and Maven-specific signing. Retain local-install instructions.
findings.closure: The README describes the existing local source pipeline without claiming Maven Central publication, a successful remote workflow, a published tag or a signing mechanism not inspected here.

findings.title: Java mediated calls are assigned to the wrong output channel
findings.difference: Three contracts say mediated fetch/secret requests and script logs go to stderr. RuntimeHost preserves the original System.out as its JSON protocol channel; OctopusHost.call sends requests through that preserved channel. Only ordinary script stdout and log values are directed to stderr.
findings.correction: In all three contracts, document fetch/secret requests on the preserved stdout JSON channel, replies on stdin, and ordinary script output/logs on stderr.
findings.closure: All three Side Effects sections describe the actual channel split without changing the runner protocol.

findings.title: C# reporting uses five attempts, not a five-retry budget
findings.difference: The contract calls the report budget five safe retries. ReportAttempts is 5 and WithRetriesAsync permits another call only while n + 1 < ReportAttempts: at most five total attempts, comprising an initial call and four retries. Stale/non-retryable failures stop sooner.
findings.correction: Use “at most five total attempts (up to four retries), with a stable task-derived key.”
findings.closure: The documented terminology distinguishes the initial attempt from retries; no runtime failure is inferred.
